obligation: CIRCIA (Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act of 2022)
basis: Final rule not published; counsel's memo lists it as pending. If finalized as proposed, the company would be covered: it exceeds the SBA size standard (800 employees for NAICS 335311) and the proposed sector criterion reaches electrical equipment manufacturing (NAICS 335) regardless of size. A voluntary CISA report is used until then

obligation: ICTS supply chain: connected vehicles rule
basis: The company makes no connected vehicles, vehicle connectivity systems or automated driving systems

obligation: EAR recordkeeping and restricted-party screening
basis: Exports of EAR99 products and technology (about 9% of revenue) to Canada, Mexico, the Caribbean and Central America; export records must be kept 5 years and export orders screened against restricted-party lists

obligation: DFARS 252.204-7012 and CMMC
basis: No DoD contracts or subcontracts and no CUI; the bid review gate declined a DFARS flow-down request in 2026-04. A CUI enclave decision is on the board's 2027 agenda

obligation: NERC CIP-013-2 supply chain risk management (direct applicability)
basis: Applies to the Responsible Entities in section 4.1; the company is not on the NERC compliance registry. Its duties arrive only through the utility addenda

obligation: Utility Supplier Cyber Security Addenda (CIP-013-2 R1 Part 1.2 flow-down)
citation: 88 utility purchase agreements, addendum secs. 1 to 6
basis: 88 utilities that operate medium or high impact BES Cyber Systems added addenda: incident notice within 24 hours (27) or 48 hours (61), access-revocation notice within 1 business day, vulnerability disclosure within 30 days, hashes or signatures for every release, and utility-controlled remote access. These are contract terms, not NERC requirements

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incidents)
basis: Publicly traded SEC registrant, not a smaller reporting company. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: SEC Regulation S-K Item 106 (risk management, strategy and governance)
basis: Same registrant status; the FY2025 Form 10-K includes Item 1C

obligation: Internal control over financial reporting (IT general controls)
basis: SEC registrant; IT general controls over the ERP, HR and payroll are tested by the SOX program and not repeated in the gap analysis

obligation: FAR 52.204-21 Basic safeguarding of covered contractor information systems
basis: All 11 civilian federal contracts include the clause; they are built to agency specifications (not COTS) and FCI resides in the ERP and labeled project sites. Awards under an agency FAR Part 40 class deviation carry FAR 52.240-93 with the same 15 requirements

obligation: FAR 52.204-25 Covered telecommunications and video surveillance equipment
basis: In all 11 federal contracts; report within 1 business day, then 10 business days

obligation: FAR 52.204-23 Kaspersky covered articles
basis: In all 11 federal contracts; report within 3 business days, then 10 business days

obligation: FAR 52.204-30 FASCSA orders
basis: Included in the 8 contracts awarded since 2024; SAM.gov review at least once every three months and reports within 3 business days

obligation: DOE certification and records for distribution transformers
basis: Distribution transformers are covered equipment; efficiency is certified by testing and certification reports and test data must be kept, organized for DOE review, for 2 years after a model is discontinued

obligation: SL-1 subscription agreements and SL-2 member agreements
basis: SL-1: 99.5% monthly availability, confidentiality, advisories within 24 hours of a high-severity alert, 72-hour data incident notice. SL-2: dispatch decision within 24 hours, accurate records, confidentiality, 72-hour data incident notice and immediate outage notices; 5 members asked for a SOC 2 Type 2 report by 2027-12-31

obligation: Tier 1 supplier security addenda (inbound incident notice)
basis: Tier 1 suppliers must notify the company within 72 hours of confirming an incident affecting company systems, data or supplied components; the TMU contract manufacturer has no signed addendum

obligation: Cyber insurance policy notice terms
basis: Notice through the carrier hotline before incident vendors are engaged

obligation: State breach notification and data security laws
citation: Each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Employee and applicant personal information in at least 6 states; notify under the law of each state of residence

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (worked example)
basis: Headquarters and most employees are in Florida, so the company holds personal information of Florida residents

obligation: Sanctions check before any ransom payment
basis: Applies to all U.S. persons; ransom requires CEO, General Counsel and insurer approval

obligation: Federal equal employment opportunity laws applied to AI hiring tools
basis: The company is an employer with 12,000 employees, and the applicant tracking system has an applicant ranking feature switched on

obligation: State and local automated employment decision and AI laws (for example Colorado, Illinois, New York City)
basis: No operations or employees in those places; counsel tracks new laws in the six states where the company operates

obligation: HIPAA Privacy, Security and Breach Notification Rules
basis: The company is not a covered entity or business associate; the employee health plan is a separate entity handled by the benefits program

obligation: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
basis: Customers pay by bank transfer; no payment card acceptance

obligation: Form DOE-417 electric emergency incident and disturbance report
basis: The form applies to electric utilities and the other entities named in its instructions, not to equipment manufacturers
